exposure: residence in service area (icddr,b vs government)
cohort: The participants were pregnant women observed prospectively from 2005 to 2019 in two Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health service areas in Matlab, Bangladesh.
finding: The proportion of caesarean section births rose dramatically from 5.9% in 2005 to 55.7% in 2019 in rural Bangladesh, with associations found for residence, age, assets, parity, and schooling, where some disparities converged while others widened over time.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates in rural Bangladesh increased ninefold (from 5.9% to 55.7%) between 2005 and 2019, with sociodemographic disparities related to maternal age, education, and place of delivery converging, while disparities related to parity and asset score persisted and widened.
